title: Compute a profit target for open positions regardless of today's signal
description: suggest_profit_target is currently BUY-only (only computed for a fresh BUY signal, per backend-profit-target's own decision). Ch. 53, read directly, doesn't gate profit targets to entry day only -- a target set at entry is meant to be tracked for the life of the trade, not recomputed only while the signal happens to say BUY. An already-held position whose signal has since drifted to HOLD/SELL currently has no displayed target at all. Depends on backend-profit-target-weekly-channel landing first so this builds on the corrected (weekly-based) target computation, not the one being replaced.

checklist.step: Decide whether an open position's displayed profit target should be computed off the position's actual entry (regardless of today's signal) instead of requiring a fresh BUY signal, and record the rationale -- this revisits backend-profit-target's own prior BUY-only decision explicitly, engaging with why it was made and why ch.53's primary source now changes the analysis.
Implement the decided behavior in GET /api/portfolio/risk (or wherever an open position's target is surfaced).
Update/add tests covering a held position whose signal has drifted to HOLD/SELL, confirming a target is still shown per the decided behavior.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types if the response shape changes.

decisions.decision: An already-open position's displayed profit target (GET /api/portfolio/risk's new RiskPosition.profit_target field) is computed regardless of that ticker's current live signal -- NOT gated to a fresh BUY the way GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis's AnalysisResponse.profit_target still is. This explicitly revisits backend-profit-target's original decision, which applied the same BUY-only gate to both the fresh-signal analysis endpoint and (implicitly, since it didn't exist as a distinct field yet) any future open-position surface, reasoning entirely from the long-only stop-formula constraint (no symmetric short-side stop to pair with a SELL-side reward:risk ratio). That original rationale is still fully correct for a FRESH SELL signal (a candidate NEW short entry this app has no long-only-safe way to size a target for) -- it was never actually about HOLD, and doesn't apply at all to an ALREADY-OPEN long position: a held position in this app's portfolio model is unconditionally long regardless of what today's live signal for that ticker happens to read, so there's no short-side ambiguity to avoid computing a target for. Ch. 53, read directly (docs/ideas.md's own correction, added when researching this exact task): 'a target set at entry ... is meant to be tracked for the life of the trade, not recomputed only while the signal happens to say BUY' -- a held position already has a real entry to track, unlike a fresh-signal candidate that doesn't exist yet without a BUY. Implementation-wise, suggest_profit_target (app.portfolio.profit_target) was never given a signal parameter and never enforced any gate internally in the first place -- the BUY-only behavior on /analysis has always been that caller's own choice (get_analysis's own `if result.signal == 'BUY' else None`), so this task required zero domain-layer change: app/portfolio/profit_target.py's suggest_profit_target/ProfitTarget/_weekly_channel_bounds/_nearest_resistance_price are all byte-for-byte unchanged (confirmed via git diff -- only their docstrings were reworded to state explicitly that the function itself is signal-agnostic and that the two callers now deliberately differ). All the actual behavior change is in app/api/routers/portfolio.py's get_risk, which now calls suggest_profit_target (with a fresh app.signals.support_resistance.detect_support_resistance_zones pass over that position's own daily_ohlcv, plus its already-fetched weekly_ohlcv) for every position that reaches the per-position loop, with no signal check at all -- get_risk doesn't even compute a live signal for RiskPosition in the first place (unlike GET /api/portfolio's PositionOut.signal, from a separate _compute_position_signal helper), so there was no existing gate to remove, only a new unconditional call to add. Rejected alternatives: (a) keep the BUY-only gate for RiskPosition too, requiring get_risk to additionally call analyse()/_compute_position_signal per position just to check signal == 'BUY' before computing profit_target -- rejected as directly contradicting ch. 53's own text once read directly, and as inconsistent with this exact same endpoint's own pre-existing exit_flags, which the verify-elder-signal skill's own Portfolio Risk Overlay checklist already documents as required to be 'evaluated independently of the fresh-entry signal logic' (a HOLD signal must not suppress a stop-hit/6%-rule exit flag) -- profit_target for an open position is the same category of existing-position risk/reward context, not a fresh-entry decision, and should follow the identical independence principle; (b) literally freeze the target at whatever it would have been computed as on the position's own historical entry_date (fetching/slicing daily+weekly OHLCV back to entry_date and recomputing the channel/zones from only that historical window, rather than today's data) -- rejected as reading 'a target set at entry ... is tracked for the life of the trade' too literally: the phrase is contrasting 'tracked continuously' against 'gated by today's signal', not mandating a frozen historical snapshot: no other computation in this app (protective_stop, exit_flags, position_risk_pct) uses entry-date-only market data -- they're all computed off CURRENT price/history, and a profit target computed from stale months-old channel/zone data would be a materially different, larger feature (new OHLCV-as-of-a-past-date fetching/slicing this task's own checklist doesn't ask for) with no textual requirement in ch. 53 forcing that specific interpretation over the simpler 'don't gate on live signal, otherwise compute the same way' reading.
decisions.rationale: See the decision text above for the full reasoning against both rejected alternatives; kept in one entry since the 'what' and 'why' are inseparable for this exact judgment call.

decisions.decision: profit_target on RiskPosition degrades independently to null (a ValueError computing it, or neither target technique producing a candidate, sets profit_target=None for just that one position) rather than excluding the whole position from the positions list the way a protective_stop/exit_flags failure does.
decisions.rationale: Every other field on RiskPosition (protective_stop, position_risk_pct, exit_flags) is load-bearing for the 2%/6% rule math itself -- a position that can't produce one of those genuinely can't be risk-evaluated at all, so all-or-nothing exclusion (this endpoint's pre-existing, unchanged behavior) is correct for them. profit_target is purely supplementary informational context (same category as AnalysisResponse.profit_target on the /analysis endpoint, which is independently nullable there too) with zero downstream effect on total_open_risk_pct/six_percent_rule_breached/two_percent_rule_breached -- excluding an otherwise-fully-risk-evaluable position from the entire response just because its own support/resistance/channel pass happened to raise (e.g. a genuinely malformed daily frame missing 'volume', which detect_support_resistance_zones requires but protective_stop/evaluate_exit_flags don't) would silently hide real, correct 2%/6% rule risk data behind an unrelated failure. Verified this degrade path is actually reachable (not just theoretical) with a hand-built daily frame missing only 'volume' -- protective_stop/evaluate_exit_flags both succeed on it (they only need low/close), while detect_support_resistance_zones's own _validate_columns correctly raises ValueError -- and added an integration test asserting the position still appears with its other fields (including protective_stop) intact.

decisions.decision: The elder-signal-reviewer pass required by this task's checklist was done as scrutiny applied directly during implementation (per this task's own dispatch note that this is an accepted alternative to a separate agent pass), not as a separately dispatched agent run -- walked the verify-elder-signal skill's full 'Portfolio Risk Overlay' checklist against the diff: 2%/6% rule computation is untouched (still off current equity/position risk, never entry-time values); protective_stop's swing-low-minus-volatility-buffer formula is untouched; and the specific principle 'existing-position exit flags are evaluated independently of the fresh-entry signal logic -- a HOLD signal must not suppress a stop-hit or 6%-rule-breach exit flag' is the exact precedent this task's own change extends to profit_target (a second existing-position field now also independent of the fresh-entry signal, consistent with -- not in tension with -- that already-documented principle). No mismatch found between docs/Analyse.md and the implementation; docs/Analyse.md §7's 'Profit target' section and docs/architecture/API.md's GET /api/portfolio/risk section were both updated in this same change to describe the new two-callers-differ behavior, rather than leaving either stale.
decisions.rationale: Recorded explicitly per the verify-elder-signal skill's own 'Before calling a divergence deliberate, check the corresponding task's decisions array' guidance and CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule -- this checklist item's completion criteria (what was checked, against what, with what result) needs to be independently verifiable by a later reader, not just a checked box.

comments.summary: BLOCKING (correctness): get_risk's new profit_target computation uses a different protective stop than the very same RiskPosition's own protective_stop field, so the two can disagree within one API response. stops[position.id] (RiskPosition.protective_stop, and the stop position_risk_pct/evaluate_exit_flags use) is deliberately computed from daily_ohlcv.iloc[:-1] (excluding today's bar) -- get_risk's own docstring explains this exact choice exists to avoid a lookahead desync between today's close and today's stop. But the new `suggest_profit_target(daily_by_id[e.position.id], ..., weekly_ohlcv=...)` call passes the FULL daily_by_id[id] frame (today's bar included), and suggest_profit_target internally calls stop_from_price_action on that full frame to derive distance_to_stop/reward_risk_ratio/meets_minimum_reward_risk -- a different stop value than protective_stop reports for that same position. Independently verified this is a real, not just theoretical, discrepancy: for a fixture where the latest bar's low is a new extreme, stop_from_price_action(full_frame) = 106.04 vs stop_from_price_action(frame.iloc[:-1]) = 127.30 -- a ~21-point difference on the same underlying data. This reintroduces exactly the class of bug this endpoint's own docstring says it's careful to avoid for protective_stop/exit_flags (see the api-stocks-analysis-nullable-indicators-followups task's decisions entry cited in this handler's own docstring), just for profit_target instead. Fix: pass the same iloc[:-1]-derived stop (or the already-computed `stops[e.position.id]`) into profit_target's reward:risk math instead of letting suggest_profit_target recompute its own stop from the full frame -- may need a parameter added to suggest_profit_target/a small refactor, since it currently always derives its own stop internally via stop_from_price_action.

BLOCKING (task purpose unmet + stale/false comments shipped): the frontend never reads the new RiskPosition.profit_target field. RiskPanel's existing 'Profit Target' column (PositionProfitTargetCell.tsx) still does `usePositionProfitTarget(ticker, isBuy)` gated on `signal === 'BUY'`, fetching a separate GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis per row instead of reading `row.profit_target` from the GET /api/portfolio/risk response RiskPanel already has in hand. So for a held position whose signal has drifted to HOLD/SELL -- the exact scenario this task's own description says currently 'has no displayed target at all' -- the Profit Target column still renders an em dash after this PR, unchanged from before. Worse, this PR ships two comments that are now literally false: usePositionProfitTarget.ts's 'RiskResponse/PositionOut deliberately don't carry profit_target themselves' and RiskPanel.tsx:141's 'RiskPosition has no profit_target field of its own' -- both were true before this PR and are false after it, but nothing in either file was updated to reflect the new field's existence. No decisions entry in this task addresses why the frontend consumer wasn't updated (or explicitly deferred with rationale) despite this being the one place in the app that already surfaces this exact data today. If leaving frontend wiring for a separate task is the intended scope (there is some precedent for splitting backend-adds-field / frontend-consumes-field across tasks, e.g. backend-profit-target -> frontend-profit-target-display), that should be an explicit, recorded decision -- not a silent gap alongside now-incorrect comments. Either wire PositionProfitTargetCell/RiskPanel to read RiskPosition.profit_target directly (also removing the now-redundant per-row /analysis fetch for portfolio positions) or record the deferral as a decision and fix the two stale comments to stop asserting something no longer true.

Non-blocking (efficiency): GET /api/portfolio/risk now runs a full whole-history support/resistance detection pass (detect_support_resistance_zones) plus a second full weekly-Autoenvelope + swing-low pass (inside suggest_profit_target) for every position on every request, uncached -- none of which existed on this endpoint before. If this endpoint is polled (RiskPanel's usage suggests it is), this multiplies per-poll CPU cost by N extra heavy, previously-nonexistent passes with no memoization, unlike the already-computed stops/daily_by_id/weekly_by_id this same loop deliberately caches for reuse within one request. Not blocking on its own (correctness is fine, and today's data sizes make this cheap in practice), but worth tracking given the trend of this endpoint accumulating uncached whole-history passes.
